report: Lahore's smog: the year-round baseline, and what changes in October

evidence.claim: PAQI: Lahore October mean PM2.5 136.3 (2025) -> 100.1 µg/m³ (2026), -27%, at 26 sites reporting in both years; PAQI model: this October's weather alone lowered PM2.5 about 19% versus last October's weather
evidence.source: PAQI analysis as reported by ProPakistani, 2 Nov 2026
evidence.note: Matched-site PAQI figures, not IQAir's 124 and 100. The earlier claim of 31 days above 35 is no longer used. Counterfactual: this October's emissions under last October's weather; with typical weather in both months the gap would be about 4% (ProPakistani).
evidence.status: verified against press report; PAQI's model not reproduced

evidence.claim: Lahore AQI 448 on Sunday 1 Nov 2026 (PMD sources, The Nation); IQAir US AQI 535 at 8 am on 2 Nov 2026 (Dawn)
evidence.source: The Nation, 2 Nov 2026; Dawn, 2 Nov 2026

evidence.claim: Lahore monthly mean PM2.5 (µg/m³), IQAir city history (one product, two readings)

limits.note: 35 is a 24-hour standard shown on a monthly chart for context; monthly means can't give daily exceedance counts

evidence.source: IQAir Lahore city page, Historic > Monthly. Oct 2025-Aug 2026 read 2026-09-14 (report/data/iqair-citypage-monthly-oct2025-sep2026.json); Sep-Oct 2026 read 2026-11-02T20:36Z (report/data/iqair-citypage-monthly-snapshot-2026-11-03.json); Dec 2025-Aug 2026 identical in both readings
evidence.not_used: IQAir 2025 annual-report city table (different, finalized product): Oct 123.4, Nov 183.9, Dec 171 (report/data/iqair-annual-and-2025-monthly.json). Earlier draft used Sep 45.6, which covered 1-14 Sep only.

evidence.claim: ERA5 boundary-layer height and 10 m wind at central Lahore, monthly means 2019-2025
evidence.source: ERA5 via Open-Meteo archive API (models=era5), hourly, 31.55 N 74.34 E
evidence.note: An earlier version of this report gave October wind speeds from Open-Meteo's default blended series, in km/h mislabelled as m/s; that series changes model in recent years. ERA5 alone shows no unusual October wind in 2025 or 2026.

evidence.claim: Hotspot detections of all kinds, all satellites, in the frame 30.0-32.6 N, 72.4-75.9 E, per Pakistan-time day
evidence.source: NASA FIRMS via HamariHawa /api/day
evidence.definition: All hotspot kinds (crop, kiln, urban, industrial, landfill, hotspot, forest, open, mixed), all satellites (Suomi NPP, NOAA-20, NOAA-21, MODIS Terra, MODIS Aqua), inside the rectangular frame 30.0-32.6 N, 72.4-75.9 E (no radius filter), per Pakistan-time day. crop_associated gives the subset with kind = crop for the two days quoted in the report. Processing: FIRMS VIIRS (low-confidence detections dropped) and MODIS (confidence >= 30); the same ~400 m spot seen by several satellites on one Pakistan-time day is counted once; MODIS points dropped where VIIRS saw a fire within ~1 km. Each detection is classified by kind (crop, kiln, urban, industrial, landfill, hotspot = persistent always-hot spot, forest, open, mixed); 'crop' = on farmland away from known kilns, dumps, industry and towns (an inference, not ground-checked). Detections are not deduplicated fire events, burned area or emissions; clouds and data gaps are not corrected.

Distances are great-circle (haversine) from 31.55 N, 74.34 E, Earth radius 6,371 km; see radius_filtering. Detections are not deduplicated fire events, burned area or emissions; clouds and data gaps are not corrected.

evidence.claim: NOAA-20 crop-fire spots within 100 km of central Lahore, Pakistani side, by period: 1-14 Oct, 15 Oct-1 Nov, 2-15 Nov, 16-30 Nov
evidence.source: HamariHawa archive (NASA FIRMS)
evidence.definition: NOAA-20 only (VIIRS, low confidence dropped; no MODIS and no other VIIRS satellite), crop-associated detections (kind = crop), districts in Pakistan only, within 100 km (haversine) of central Lahore; periods 1-14 Oct, 15 Oct-1 Nov, 2-15 Nov, 16-30 Nov, Pakistan time; the same ~400 m spot on one day counted once. after_1_nov_share_pct = (2-15 Nov + 16-30 Nov) / 1 Oct-30 Nov total. Distances are great-circle (haversine) from 31.55 N, 74.34 E, Earth radius 6,371 km; see radius_filtering. Kinds as in timelapse_counts; not fire events, burned area or emissions.

evidence.source: HamariHawa archive (NASA FIRMS)
evidence.definition: NOAA-20 only, crop-associated detections (kind = crop) in districts of Indian Punjab state (whole state, no radius filter), counted per Pakistan-time day, 1 Oct-30 Nov; the peak day is the day with the most detections (2026: archive to 2 Nov). Daily counts attached. Not fire events, burned area or emissions. Clouds and data gaps are not corrected.
evidence.status: reproduced from archive (exact match, 3 Nov 2026); Diwali dates are calendar facts, not checked against the archive
evidence.note: Detections in Indian Punjab have fallen since 2021, but NASA reports a shift to later-afternoon burning after satellite overpasses, so fewer detections need not mean less burning. No causal claim about Diwali.

evidence.claim: Tropospheric NO2, mean of 15 Oct-1 Nov, Lahore box 31.40-31.65 N 74.20-74.45 E vs farmland box 31.0-31.3 N 73.8-74.1 E
evidence.source: Copernicus Sentinel-5P TROPOMI via NASA GIBS (TROPOMI_L2_Nitrogen_Dioxide_Tropospheric_Column), processed by HamariHawa
evidence.caveat: values read back from GIBS colour bands (quantized to about one band); valid observations per city pixel about 6.2 (2023), 18 (2024), 18 (2025), 7.1 (2026): 2024-25 tiles have a markedly different coverage pattern (a value every day), cause not established; the ~10% 2026-vs-2023 difference is not treated as a trend. Imagery usable here from 2023; TROPOMI record starts 2018.
evidence.status: arithmetic verified; product version per year not documented by GIBS layer

evidence.claim: HamariHawa NO2 hotspots, 14 days to 1 Nov 2026, Pakistan: Rawalpindi 6.43, Karachi 5.82, Lahore south-centre (31.494, 74.344) 4.68 (ratio to surroundings)
evidence.source: https://hamarihawa.org/api/no2.json
evidence.note: HamariHawa relative-enrichment ranking (column vs surroundings), 14 days to 1 Nov 2026; not an official ranking of ground-level concentrations

evidence.claim: Lahore registered vehicles 30 Sep 2024: 7,484,203 (motorcycles 5,234,187; cars 1,677,740; rickshaws 228,508; pickups/vans 130,827; tractors 68,595; buses 56,957; trucks 44,127; taxis 27,573); Punjab 24,533,994. About 15,000 heavy vehicles enter Lahore daily (traffic police via Dawn, 3 Dec 2022). Punjab 2020 road exhaust PM2.5 (kt/yr): heavy-duty and buses 17.62, motorcycles 5.78, cars 4.32, light-duty 4.25; tyre/brake 2.20, road abrasion 2.45. NOx (kt): heavy 219.3, cars 90.5, light-duty 25.3, motorcycles 3.8
evidence.geography: registrations: Lahore district; emissions: all of Punjab, 2020
evidence.status: verified (Excise PDF, Annex B); wording corrected
evidence.note: Registrations don't measure vehicles operating in Lahore. EMEP/EEA diesel-vs-four-stroke comparison is of technology-category factors, not a measured Lahore fleet ratio. Lahore inventory: CO about 80% of transport emission mass (not a motorcycle-specific breakdown).

evidence.claim: Euro V for imported petrol from Aug 2020 and diesel from Jan 2021; local refineries (May 2025): one Euro V, two Euro III, others high-sulphur diesel; Brownfield refinery policy (2023, amended Feb 2024 and Aug 2026): completion within five years of signing the Upgrade Agreement, extendable by cure period (max one year cumulative), force majeure, or a further one year case by case (§6.1.3.5, §6.1.4.1); ECC approved the Upgrade Agreement with a five-year completion period on 14 Sep 2026 (PID PR 146), tariff incentives seven years (§6.1.2.2); new vehicles Euro II
evidence.status: corrected (was: about seven years to upgrade)
evidence.note: 'Notified 10 Sep 2026' could not be confirmed from the policy or PID release

evidence.claim: Brick kilns within 25 / 50 km of central Lahore, Pakistani side
evidence.source: site/public/sources/kilns.json (SentinelKilnDB CC BY-NC 4.0; Brick Kiln Dataset for Pakistan's IGP Region CC BY 4.0)
evidence.dedup: two datasets merged; points within about 60 m merged (scripts/build-sources.py build_kilns); within 50 km (both sides) 1,022 points remain, 71 pairs under 100 m apart and 186 under 200 m, so a few may be duplicates
evidence.note: mapped features, not a census of operating kilns
evidence.status: corrected (was 894/197; the earlier side-assignment method could not be reproduced); deduplication imperfect

evidence.claim: Within 50 km: 7 oil/gas power plants, five to the west/north-west around Sheikhupura (Bhikki about 1,180 MW per NEPRA, Sapphire 235, Halmore 225, Atlas 214, Saba 134) and two near Raiwind (Kohinoor 131, Reshma); 181 OSM industrial areas within 50 km on the Pakistani side (214 within 50 km in total)
evidence.source: site/public/sources/city/lahore.json (OpenStreetMap); https://ppib.gov.pk/bhikki.html
evidence.operational_note: Atlas Power Limited and Saba Power Company: PPAs terminated effective 30 Sep 2024 (CPPA-G Annual Report 2025, printed p.42; Dawn 11 Oct 2024). Operating status of the others not checked; locations and contract status don't establish operation or emissions.
evidence.status: industrial count reproduced (181); PPA dates verified; operation not verified

evidence.claim: Closed 2016; about 14 million tonnes on about 41 acres; covered with soil, vent pipes installed; LWMC: gas to be sold to industry if enough, burnt if not; as of March 2025 methane releasing slowly from vents; Lakhodair takes about 5,000 t/day
evidence.source: BBC Urdu, Umar Draz Nangiana, 24 Mar 2025

evidence.claim: NASA fire detections within 450 m of the Mehmood Booti mound centre (31.6104, 74.3847), archived Oct-Nov season days
evidence.source: HamariHawa archive (NASA FIRMS)
evidence.definition: Detections of any kind from any satellite (Suomi NPP, NOAA-20, NOAA-21, MODIS Terra, MODIS Aqua) within 450 m (haversine, Earth radius 6,371 km) of the Mehmood Booti mound centre 31.6104 N, 74.3847 E, Pakistan-time days 1 Oct-30 Nov each season (2026: 1 Oct-2 Nov, 33 days). No crop/kind filter: all seven detections found are classified 'landfill' and all are VIIRS (Suomi NPP or NOAA-20). Same archive processing (low-confidence VIIRS dropped, one detection per ~400 m spot per day). Heat seen nearby but beyond 450 m (e.g. neighbouring sites within ~1 km) is not counted here. Not fire events or emissions; clouds and data gaps are not corrected, and small, short-lived, smoke-obscured or underground fires can be missed.

evidence.claim: Sentinel-2 clear passes (cloud <15%) Oct 2024-Nov 2026 over the Lakhodair dump surface (31.619-31.636 N, 74.413-74.424 E): 86; passes with any pixel B12>0.45: 5; the two large ones (21 Aug 2025, 8 Oct 2026) were clouds on inspection; the others 2-10 pixels
evidence.source: Earth Search Sentinel-2 L2A COGs, processed by HamariHawa
evidence.status: unverified count; text no longer gives a number
evidence.reproduction: The original 86 scenes were not archived. Re-listing on 3 Nov 2026 (Earth Search STAC, sentinel-2-l2a, dump box, scene-level eo:cloud_cover < 15, 1 Oct 2024-2 Nov 2026) gives 184 items on 99 distinct dates: report/data/lakhodair-s2-scenes-2026-11-03.json. Scene-level cloud cover doesn't guarantee a clear view of the site.
evidence.conclusion: No clear large surface fire identified in the usable images examined; small, short-lived, obscured or subsurface fires can be missed

evidence.claim: Carbon Mapper source record, Lakhodair: persistence-adjusted source emission estimate 1,559.3 kg CH4/h, reported uncertainty 438.3 kg/h (confidence level not stated); 19 plumes; detected on 11 of 12 observed dates (persistence 91.67%); plume detection dates 2023-06-10 to 2026-03-22. No Carbon Mapper record for Mehmood Booti
evidence.note: Carbon Mapper persistence-adjusted source estimate combining emission rates by observation date; not a continuous whole-landfill measurement. Not all detected plumes necessarily have quantified rates; uncertainty confidence level not stated.

evidence.claim: CAMS global (Open-Meteo 'dust' = aermr06, largest dust bin, particle radii 0.9-20 µm (ECMWF param 210006; radii per ECMWF forum), not total dust) daily mean >= 50 µg/m³ at 31.55 N 74.34 E on 9 days in Oct 2026 (1-3, 7-11, 30 Oct); modelled PM2.5 averaged 65.30 µg/m³ on those days and 67.67 on the other 22
evidence.method: hourly values, averaged by Pakistan-time day (timezone Asia/Karachi), 24 hours per day
evidence.source: Open-Meteo air-quality API, domains=cams_global, read 3 Nov 2026 (report/data/cams-lahore-oct2026-hourly.json); field mapping: open-meteo Sources/App/Cams/CamsDomain.swift; https://codes.ecmwf.int/grib/param-db/210006
evidence.removed: 'dust about 40-44% of modelled PM10' (one size bin is not a dust-PM10 fraction); causal conclusions about dust and AQI
evidence.pm10_definition: PM10 includes particles with aerodynamic diameters up to about 10 µm, including PM2.5

evidence.claim: Urban Unit Lahore 2023 inventory (2021 data), PM2.5 t/yr: transport 397, crop burning 371, waste burning 320, industry 29, total 1,120; transport's 83% is of all pollutants summed by mass (mostly CO); notes vehicle figures may be overestimated. PAQI national landscape report (https://zenodo.org/records/17629179; Dawn, 10 Dec 2025): Lahore primary PM2.5 emissions 35% transport, 28% heavy industry, 17% brick kilns; Punjab EPA disputes its data
evidence.note: Emission-inventory shares, not ambient or receptor apportionment; secondary formation, transport and removal prevent direct conversion

evidence.claim: Share of Dec-Jan days with daily-mean visibility < 1 km, winters with >= 70% of days reported. Amritsar airport (GSOD 42071099999): 1970s 0.8%, 1980s 4.4%, 1990s 10.3%, 2000s 13.9%, 2010s 20.0%, 2020-24 41.1%. Lahore airport (41641099999) days < 1 km per Oct-Jan winter: 1992-97 0-1; 1998-99 to 2017-18 1-23
evidence.source: NOAA NCEI Global Surface Summary of the Day
evidence.caveat: unadjusted daily-mean visibility; fog, haze and smoke not separable; changing observation frequency can shift daily means
evidence.geography: Amritsar airport about 47 km from 31.55 N 74.34 E; Lahore airport about 7 km
evidence.winter_label: Amritsar: Dec of year Y + Jan of Y+1, grouped by Y; Lahore: Oct-Jan season labelled Y-(Y+1)
evidence.observation_frequency: Amritsar median readings per day: 5-7 in 1970s-80s, 6-14 in 1990s, 10-21 in 2000s, 22-24 since 2010s; series not adjusted

evidence.claim: MODIS (Terra+Aqua, SP, conf >= 30) fires 15 Oct-30 Nov: NE Pakistani Punjab (box 29.5-32.6 N, 72.0-76.9 E) 631/670/694 in 2002-04, 1,572/1,663/1,614/1,636 in 2022-25; share of 1 Oct-30 Nov fires in November: Indian Punjab 5/10/11% (2002-04) to 78/67/83/85/73% (2021-25); Pakistani side 87/79/88% to 57/51/63/61/45%. Within 100 km of Lahore, Indian side 2.4-5.6x Pakistani side in 2009-2020, similar in 2024-25 (950 vs 750; 793 vs 683)
evidence.source: NASA FIRMS MODIS_SP C6.1, processed by HamariHawa
evidence.definition: MODIS only (Terra + Aqua, MODIS_SP Collection 6.1 standard product, confidence >= 30), all detections in the stated box or radius with no crop/kind classification and no cross-satellite deduplication, 15 Oct-30 Nov (shares: 1 Oct-30 Nov) each year 2002-2025. These are not the HamariHawa archive's classified detections, and late-afternoon burning after the satellite overpasses is missed (NASA Earth Observatory).

evidence.claim: ERA5 November mean boundary-layer height at Lahore by decade: 1980s 278 m, 1990s 298, 2000s 294, 2010s 281, 2020-25 252; Theil-Sen -7 m/decade (p 0.05); November wind about 1.85 m/s with no trend; lowest Novembers 2025 (220.0 m), 1987 (226.1), 2023 (230.9), 2016 (233.8); OLS trend -6.2 m/decade (about -10% over 1980-2025), interannual SD 29 m; November mean 10 m wind 1.86 (1980s) vs 1.88 m/s (last 10 years)
evidence.source: ERA5 via Open-Meteo (models=era5), 1980-2025
evidence.note: all-hour means, not afternoon depths; 2025 and 2023 Novembers had conditions favouring accumulation near the ground; humidity and other variables not analysed

evidence.claim: Lahore annual PM2.5 194 ± 94 µg/m³, Jan 2007-Jan 2008 (Stone et al. 2010); fog frequency regime shifts ~1990 and ~1998 over South Asia (Syed et al. 2012); Lahore district population 6.32 m (1998), 13.00 m (2023); Lahore registered vehicles ~1.95 m (2008, JICA)
evidence.note: Stone et al. 2010: PM2.5 194 ± 94 µg/m³, samples every sixth day 12 Jan 2007-19 Jan 2008; one study, not comparable with modern network means for trends. Syed et al. 2012: 82 stations 1976-2010, fog regime shifts 1990 and 1998, alongside gradual RH rise (abstract via search snippets; publisher page blocked). Dawn 30 Dec 2008 on Suparco fog study. JICA 2012: 1.95 m motorized vehicles registered in Lahore in 2008. IRIN Dec 2006 'smog' article could not be opened, so not cited.
evidence.status: verified (Stone abstract, Dawn, JICA); Syed via abstract snippets

status_key.verified: checked against the primary source, or recomputed from an archived input on 3 Nov 2026
status_key.reproduced from archive: recomputed exactly from HamariHawa's archived FIRMS-derived day files (extract attached); the archive's processing of raw FIRMS files was not independently re-audited
status_key.arithmetic_only: arithmetic checked; underlying observations not re-checked
status_key.unverified: not reproduced; precision removed or limitation stated

radius_filtering: The km_from_31.55N_74.34E column in the fire CSVs is rounded to 0.1 km for display. To reproduce the reported counts, recompute each detection's great-circle (haversine) distance from its lat/lon to 31.55 N, 74.34 E with Earth radius 6,371 km and filter on that. Filtering the rounded column directly gives different boundary counts: 785 instead of 781 within 40 km and 7,148 instead of 7,130 within 100 km (15 Oct-1 Nov 2026, kind = crop). fires-noaa20-crop-pk-100km-2019-2026.csv is already filtered to <= 100 km by haversine distance. Mehmood Booti uses the same formula from 31.6104 N, 74.3847 E.
